items.title: Bernie Kirsh interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 27, 2022
items.q: I mean there would be Carly Simon opening for Kris Kristofferson, you know it was that era, but major acts.

ctx.x: Yeah. But at some point did you start hearing ways of recording music that you noticed and then what made you enter this world?

Happenstance. I had no interest — well back up a little bit. When I was in college I actually turned into a theater major and got involved in technical theater, did all the other things that a theater student would do — acting, directing, and so forth. But then got an offer for a graduate assistantship in technical theater: building sets and that sort of thing. So I went to graduate school doing that and while I was there I got involved in the television station at the school. And of course I had my theater…

you know. And so I went over there every day for a couple of weeks. I was working nights of course, at the club, and during the day I would just go over there and spend hours just sitting in the back of the room watching what was going on, and got interested. I got interested in the process, in working with musicians, which I had been doing at the club, but I love musicians. And you know it’s my group, my people. And so it was a way for me to interact with them. I wasn’t playing anymore, I really wasn’t playing…
